A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynShot research work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar reconstruction and reenactment experiments, quantitative frame-count evaluations, architecture and loss ablations, and supplementary failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and ablations and adds qualitative and quantitative comparisons with animatable GAN-based methods.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE prior, identity/expression branches, per-part Gaussian regression, training objectives, and two-stage pivotal tuning remain unchanged. Figure 2 corrects swapped latent labels and expands the explanation; it does not establish an architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the synthetic training data, eleven monocular sequences, Preface hair/beard examples, and reconstruction, novel-view, and reenactment tasks. The new GAN comparisons use retained task coverage. FFHQ is newly discussed in relation to prior work, without evidence of an added experimental dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds actual self- and cross-reenactment comparisons with InvertAvatar, Portrait4D, and Next3D, substantially expanding evaluation against animatable generative priors. INSTA, FlashAvatar, SplattingAvatar, HeadNeRF, MofaNeRF, and PanoHead remain represented across the main text and appendix.

E3.justification: The added GAN comparison introduces an explicit input-budget arrangement: three images for SynShot and InvertAvatar, versus one for Portrait4D and Next3D. The retained monocular evaluation is not shown to have changed; specifying its last-600-frame test selection adds documentation.

E4.justification: v2 removes the standalone three-versus-987-frame novel-view comparison in v1 Figure 7 and one subject's qualitative frame-count sweep in v1 Figure 21. Architecture and loss ablations, aggregate frame-count sensitivity, other qualitative sweeps, and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 600 frames across 11 subjects in the retained reconstruction plots. No new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds GAN comparison results, including LPIPS scores of 0.0236 for SynShot, 0.0962 for InvertAvatar, 0.0843 for Portrait4D, and 0.2274 for Next3D, alongside new qualitative reenactment results in Figures 8 and 10. These are newly reported comparisons under their stated input budgets. Existing ablation values and retained frame-count curves are unchanged, while some qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, quantization rule, Gaussian parameterization, losses, and appendix splatting formulas are retained. Notation and diagram-label corrections do not alter the mathematical reasoning, and neither version introduces formal proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the performance claim from monocular methods to monocular and GAN-based methods. It also makes consent and data-regulation burdens an explicit third challenge. The two central technical contributions and the conclusion's synthetic-prior claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains that benefiting from additional input frames requires more fine-tuning iterations and links iteration budgets to non-monotonic LPIPS behavior. The limitations concerning teeth, wrinkles, lighting, glasses, eyes, and missing hairstyles remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the self-reenactment test frames as the last 600 frames from the INSTA dataset, supplies per-actor inversion inputs in Figure 22, and explicitly identifies regularized spherical-harmonic components as l >= 1. These are documentation additions; the established hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning against Portrait4D, Next3D, and InvertAvatar, plus citations for FFHQ/StyleGAN and PointNet++. It discusses identity and novel-view weaknesses of GAN-based priors while retaining the existing related-work categories and central synthetic-prior positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are expanded, related-work passages are revised, and the results narrative adds an Evaluation paragraph and GAN-based comparison subsection while dropping the dedicated single-image discussion. Most method prose, limitations, conclusion, and appendix explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: The main results presentation is substantially reorganized around two new GAN comparison panels. Several earlier panels are removed or condensed, Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer and corrected labels, existing figures and tables are relocated, and an inversion-input montage is added to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added animatable-prior baselines make the evaluation more relevant to SynShot's central claims. Corrected pipeline labels, explicit input images, and clearer test-selection details improve assessability. These gains outweigh the limited loss of qualitative analyses, although unequal input budgets and limited quantitative reporting constrain the strength of the new comparison.
